name: IgG4-related Mesenteritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: IgG4-Related Disease Comprehensive Diagnostic Criteria (2011) adapted for mesenteritis

criteria.description: Characteristic histopathological features including dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate rich in IgG4-positive plasma cells, storiform fibrosis, and obliterative phlebitis in mesenteric tissue
Radiological evidence of mesenteric mass or thickening with characteristic features on CT or MRI
Exclusion of malignancy, infection, and other causes of mesenteritis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with elevated serum IgG4 and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, serological, radiological, and histopathological data.

pathognomonic.notes: Firm, often painless abdominal mass detected on physical exam
Characteristic histological pattern diagnostic of IgG4-related disease
searchTerms: fibrosis with swirling pattern under microscope

common.symptomName: Chronic abdominal pain localized to the mesenteric region
searchTerms: chronic abdominal discomfort in mesenteric area
persistent stomach pain localized to bowel region
symptoms of blocked bowel like vomiting
constipation and vomiting due to bowel blockage

rare.symptomName: Mesenteric vessel obliterative phlebitis leading to ischemia
searchTerms: blocked mesenteric veins causing poor blood flow
vein inflammation leading to bowel ischemia
blood vessel blockage in mesentery causing tissue damage

imaging: CT scan showing mesenteric mass or diffuse mesenteric thickening with delayed enhancement
MRI demonstrating characteristic fibrosis and soft tissue involvement
PET-CT may show increased uptake in affected mesenteric regions
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations reported in some populations
other: Histopathology showing dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate rich in IgG4-positive plasma cells, storiform fibrosis, and obliterative phlebitis

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of storiform fibrosis and IgG4-positive plasma cells
Typical radiological features with desmoplastic reaction
Histopathology lacks IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltration

redFlags: Signs of bowel obstruction or ischemia
Unexplained systemic symptoms such as high fever or weight loss
references: Stone JH, Zen Y, Deshpande V. IgG4-related disease. N Engl J Med. 2012 Feb 9;366(6):539-51.
Deshpande V, et al. Consensus statement on the pathology of IgG4-related disease. Mod Pathol. 2012 Sep;25(9):1181-92.
Kamisawa T, et al. IgG4-related sclerosing mesenteritis: a rare manifestation of IgG4-related disease. Intern Med. 2015;54(3):293-7.
